document_title: Outside AI Money in Alaska's Senate Race, Mapped
post_copy:
Most Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI employees who gave in Alaska's Senate race live in California. Not one lists an Alaska address.

An Alaska Beacon analysis of FEC records found at least 19 of them gave about $119,000. No Senate race this year drew more.

Inside the border, the race stood 637 votes apart in the unofficial count as of November 4th.

Peltola got at least $56,000. Sullivan got about $63,000 plus $35,000 to his leadership PAC.

Ranked choices get tabulated November 18th. The dollars came from Outside. The count that settles the seat happens inside.

Both campaigns' money on one scale and the national ranking with and without Big Tech. Then the joint committees, the Air Force land offer and the unofficial count.

Should voters weigh money from donors with no Alaska address differently than a neighbor's?

#AKSenate #CampaignFinance #AlaskaAI
deck_summary_line: Both campaigns' money on one scale and the national ranking with and without Big Tech. Then the joint committees, the Air Force land offer and the unofficial count.

slides.kicker: ALASKA'S U.S. SENATE RACE, PER AN ALASKA BEACON ANALYSIS OF FEC RECORDS
slides.headline: No Senate race drew more from AI-company employees. Zero Alaska addresses.

slides.kicker: ONE SCALE FOR EVERY DOLLAR IN THIS DECK
slides.headline: About $119,000 from at least 19 donors.
slides.body: Peltola, at least $56,000, nearly all from Anthropic employees. Sullivan, about $63,000, plus $35,000 to his True North leadership PAC that the $119,000 leaves out. Figures per the Alaska Beacon.

slides.kicker: THE TOP RACE, ON ONE SCALE
slides.headline: First among Senate races. Fifth and 14th among candidates.
slides.body: Mike Rounds of South Dakota tops the candidates at $165,100 with PACs. Sullivan's $98,000 counts his PAC. Most donors gave close to the legal limit.

slides.headline: Count Big Tech too, and the order flips.
slides.body: Counting Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI alone, Sullivan ranks 5th and Peltola 14th. Add Big Tech employees and Peltola ranks 5th, Sullivan 16th. Close to 150 Big Tech donors gave to Peltola, four to Sullivan.

slides.headline: Same map, second stream. In April the Air Force offered developers land on three Alaska bases for AI data centers.

slides.kicker: BEFORE THE LAND, THE MONEY'S ROUTE
slides.headline: Most of it moved through joint committees first.
slides.body: More than half of Peltola's came through the Fish Family Freedom Fund, and Sullivan's mainly through One Team Senate Majority and Sullivan Victory. The Beacon traced it with an AI agent called DataTalk.
labels: LIKELY ONE CHECK, TWO LINES. CORSELL'S $7,000 TO SULLIVAN VICTORY, THEN $3,500 + $3,500 MARKED TRANSFER MEMO ON THE CAMPAIGN'S FILING.

slides.headline: Same weeks, separate records.
slides.body: As the Air Force set site visits at three Alaska bases, executives of Twenty First Century Utilities and Saige Consulting appear in Sullivan's FEC filings. Employer data shouldn't be read as proof of coordinated giving, Campaign Legal Center's Brendan Fischer told the Beacon.

slides.headline: 637 votes apart, with about a quarter still to count.
slides.body: Peltola 48 percent, Sullivan 47.7 percent, 215,912 ballots counted. Ranked choices are tabulated November 18th, with certification targeted for November 25th.
labels: ROUGHLY A QUARTER NOT YET TALLIED

slides.headline: Save this for November 18th.
slides.body: At least 19 donors, none with an Alaska address. 637 votes apart. The count is still open.

editor_notes_for_email: Fairness choices. Peltola and Sullivan share one material and one 4 px per $1,000 scale on every frame. The Alaska Current's $58,000 network tally is deliberately not printed. The FEC transfer-memo entries are never added to the joint-committee receipts, and the calendar frame carries the Campaign Legal Center caveat that employer data isn't proof of coordinated giving. The 637-vote margin, the 48 to 47.7 percent split and the 215,912 ballots are the unofficial count as of Wednesday afternoon, November 4th, and are superseded by later counts, the November 18th ranked choice tabulation and certification targeted for November 25th. Disclosure, this deck was produced with Claude, made by Anthropic, whose employees are among the donors it counts.
